idiom_name: immutable typed value + validating factory + attribute-based equality
implementation_notes: Language-neutral structure: declare a type whose state is private and final, validate and normalise every argument in the constructor or a named static factory so no invalid instance can exist, and expose only behaviour that returns new values instead of mutating. Implement equality and hashing over exactly the attributes of the conceptual whole (never over caches, timestamps or derived state), keeping the two in sync, and deep-freeze or copy collection attributes so the value is immutable through and through. Provide a copy/with-style transformation for single-attribute changes and let the owning entity or aggregate persist the value with its own record, because the value has no identity, repository or lifecycle of its own.
code_sketch:
value Money                # conceptual whole: amount + currency
  create(amount, currency) # validate + normalise, reject invalid
  amount, currency: final  # private, immutable state
equal(a, b) = same type and same amount and same currency
# change one attribute -> produce a new Money, never mutate in place
pitfalls: Immutability that stops at the wrapper: referenced collections and collaborators must be immutable too, otherwise the value can still change under its holder.
Equality drifting from hashing, or equality including attributes that are not part of the conceptual whole.
Bypassing the factory (public constructor or public fields) so that invariants are never enforced.
Reflection-based equality/base class that hides which attributes actually participate in equality, making it easy to forget a field.
Floating-point NaN values that break equality contracts (NaN != NaN by IEEE 754).
Case-insensitive string comparison done inconsistently between construction and equality checking.
ORM lazy-loaded proxies wrapping your value object and breaking equality (the proxy class != the actual class, so instanceof or getClass checks fail).
JSON deserialisation bypassing the constructor and writing directly to fields, creating an object that passes equality checks but violates invariants.
sources: Vladimir Khorikov, Value Objects Explained (2015), Enterprise Craftsmanship — https://enterprisecraftsmanship.com/posts/value-objects-explained/
